params.body:
## Why

On the vehicle sheet, the block "Niet zichtbaar voor lokale dealers" lists the dealers within the
chosen radius so the user can tick who may not see the vehicle. That list contained the dealer the
vehicle belongs to, at 0,0 km and therefore at the top: Shane saw "Peugeot De Backer, Staatsbaan 35,
Adegem, 0,0 km" in his own list. A dealer cannot hide a vehicle from itself, so the row was both
meaningless and the first thing the eye lands on.

## Where the list is built

`App\Repositories\Settings\DealerRepository::getCloseDealers($radius, $vehicle_id)` — the haversine
query around `Auth::user()->dealer->latitude/longitude`, with a `checked` subquery against
`vehicle_dealer_exceptions` and ordering by distance. Two callers, both the same screen:

- `App\Http\Controllers\Settings\DealerController::get_dealers_within_radius()`, the AJAX endpoint
  `ownvehicle.show.dealers_within_range` behind the radius select of the classic sheet
  (`resources/js/vehicle/vehicle.js`, `show_dealers_within_radius`), and
- `App\Livewire\VehicleForm::dealersInRange()`, the same list in the Livewire sheet.

No other screen uses the method, so nothing depended on the own dealer being in the list.

## What changed

One condition in the query: `->where('dealers.id', '!=', $ownDealerId)`. The excluded dealer follows
the **vehicle**, not the logged-in user: `$ownDealerId` is the vehicle's `dealer_id`, falling back to
the user's dealer when the vehicle does not exist yet (the create form passes no saved row). An
administrator editing another dealer's vehicle therefore sees that dealer excluded, not their own.

The exclusion is by identity, not by distance: a second dealer at the very same address stays in the
list. The radius centre is unchanged (still the logged-in user's dealer); that is existing behaviour
and out of scope here.

## Existing rows

Rows for the own dealer may already exist in `vehicle_dealer_exceptions` from before this fix. They
are **left in place, no migration**, for two reasons:

- They are harmless. The only queries reading the table (`App\Repositories\OwnStock\VehicleRepository`,
  four places) ask "is this vehicle hidden for *my* dealer" while listing *other* dealers' Stocklist
  vehicles; own-stock and the own-dealer branch of `getForShowroom()` never consult it. A vehicle
  hidden from its own dealer is still fully visible to its owner.
- The classic sheet heals itself: saving writes the exceptions with
  `$vehicle->except_dealers()->sync(...)` (`App\Services\OwnStockService::except_dealers`), and since
  the own dealer is no longer rendered as a checkbox it drops out of the posted set on the next save.

Deleting rows in bulk the day before the cutover cannot be shown to be safe, and nothing is gained by
it.

## Checked

- Radius select: unchanged; both callers still pass the chosen radius straight through, and the
  Livewire path still maps 'no limit' (0) to a whole-earth radius.
- "Check all" header checkbox: unchanged. The classic one compares the number of ticked rows with the
  number of rendered rows (`vehicle.js`), the Livewire one (`VehicleForm::toggleAlleDealers`) works on
  the ids of `dealersInRange()`. Both now simply count one row less, so "all ticked" still means all
  rows on screen.
- Ticking/unticking writes `vehicle_dealer_exceptions` exactly as before (`sync` on the posted set);
  pinned by a test.
- Tests: `tests/Feature/CloseDealersTest.php` — the own dealer is absent while a dealer at the same
  address is still present; the excluded dealer follows the vehicle and not the logged-in user;
  ticking a dealer still stores exactly one exception row. Verified they fail when the new condition
  is removed.
- `php artisan view:cache` ok. `php artisan test --filter='Dealer|Vehicle|VehicleForm|OwnStock|SmokeTest'`
  green (271 tests) against a schema-loaded MySQL database.
params.title: Vehicle sheet: the own dealer is not in the hide-from list
